concepts.name: Downstream and upstream speeds
concepts.description: The stream helps a boat going downstream and slows it going upstream.

concepts.name: Finding still-water and stream speeds
concepts.description: From the two effective speeds you can recover both the boat and the stream.

concepts.name: Round trips
concepts.description: Total time is the sum of the two legs; average speed is not the average of the speeds.

concepts.name: Equal times and ratios
concepts.description: Setting distances or times equal gives an equation for the unknown speed.

formulas.title: Downstream and upstream
formulas.prompt: A boat with speed b in still water moves in a stream of speed s. What are its effective speeds?
formulas.formula:
Downstream = b + s
Upstream = b − s
formulas.explanation: Going with the current adds the stream; going against it subtracts.
formulas.commonMistake: Adding the stream speed in both directions.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A boat does 10 km/hr in still water and the stream flows at 4 km/hr. What is its upstream speed?

formulas.title: Recover b and s
formulas.prompt: Given downstream speed D and upstream speed U, how do you find b and s?
formulas.explanation: D + U = 2b and D − U = 2s. The boat speed is the midpoint of the two; the stream is half the gap.
formulas.commonMistake: Giving D − U as the stream speed and forgetting to halve.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Downstream 15 km/hr, upstream 9 km/hr. What is the stream speed?

formulas.title: Round-trip time
formulas.prompt: A boat goes a distance d downstream and back. What is the total time?
formulas.explanation: Each leg has its own speed, so time each leg separately and add.
formulas.commonMistake: Using the still-water speed for the whole trip.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A boat with b = 8 and s = 2 goes 30 km each way. How long is the round trip?

formulas.title: Round-trip average speed
formulas.prompt: What is the average speed over a round trip with speeds D and U?
formulas.explanation: Equal distances mean the average is weighted by time, so the harmonic form applies.
formulas.commonMistake: Taking (D + U) ÷ 2, which overweights the fast leg.
formulas.applicationPrompt: D = 12 and U = 6 km/hr. What is the round-trip average speed?

formulas.title: Distance from the round-trip time
formulas.prompt: A boat goes to a place and back in total time T. How far away is the place?
formulas.explanation: It is d/(b + s) + d/(b − s) = T, already solved for d.
formulas.example: b = 10 km/h, s = 2 km/h, T = 5 hours: 5 × 96 ÷ 20 = 24 km (2 hours down, 3 hours up).
formulas.commonMistake: Using the still-water speed for the whole trip, which gives 25 km.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A boat rows at 8 km/h in still water in a 2 km/h current and returns in 4 hours.

formulas.title: Upstream takes n times as long
formulas.prompt: Rowing a distance upstream takes n times as long as rowing it downstream. What is the ratio of boat speed to stream speed?
formulas.explanation: Downstream speed is n times upstream speed: b + s = n(b − s).
formulas.example: Upstream takes twice as long: b : s = 3 : 1.
formulas.commonMistake: Giving n : 1, the ratio of the two speeds along the river, not of boat to stream.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A swimmer takes three times as long against the current as with it.

levels.title: The Stream Adds and Subtracts
levels.description: Effective speeds, and how to get both unknowns from two numbers.

blocks.title: Two speeds, one boat
blocks.body: A boat has a still-water speed b and the stream has speed s. Going with the stream the boat is carried along: b + s. Against it, the stream holds it back: b − s.

blocks.title: Effective speeds
blocks.body:
Downstream = b + s
Upstream = b − s
blocks.caption: Then the usual distance = speed × time applies to each leg.

blocks.title: Working backwards
blocks.body: If you are told D and U, then b is their average and s is half their difference. The boat speed always sits exactly between the two effective speeds.

levels.title: Boats Formulas
levels.description: Effective speeds, recovering b and s, and round trips.

levels.title: Times and Distances
levels.description: Use times and distances to find speeds.

questions.question: A boat can go 12 km/hr in still water and the stream flows at 3 km/hr. What is its speed downstream?
questions.explanation: Downstream, the stream adds to the boat speed: 12 + 3 = 15 km/hr.
questions.method: With the current: add the stream.

hints.text: Does the current help or hinder a boat going downstream?

commonMistakes: Subtracting the stream, which gives the upstream speed.

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 10 km/hr and the stream flows at 4 km/hr. What is its speed upstream, in km/hr?
questions.method: Against the current: subtract the stream.

hints.text: Upstream means against the current.

questions.question: A boat goes downstream at 18 km/hr and upstream at 10 km/hr. What is its speed in still water?
questions.explanation: Still-water speed is the average of the two: (18 + 10) ÷ 2 = 14 km/hr.

hints.text: The stream adds in one direction and subtracts in the other. What is left when you average them?

commonMistakes: Giving the stream speed (4) or the sum (28).

questions.question: A boat's downstream speed is D and its upstream speed is U. Which expression gives the speed of the stream?
questions.explanation: D − U = 2s, because the stream is added once and subtracted once. So s = (D − U) ÷ 2.
solutionSteps: D = b + s and U = b − s.
questions.method: Half the gap between the two speeds.

hints.text: Subtract the two speeds. What remains?

questions.question: A boat goes 24 km downstream in 2 hours and returns the same distance in 4 hours. What is its speed in still water, in km/hr?
questions.explanation: Downstream = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 km/hr; upstream = 24 ÷ 4 = 6 km/hr. Still water = (12 + 6) ÷ 2 = 9 km/hr.

hints.text: First convert each leg into a speed.
Then average the two speeds.

commonMistakes: Averaging the times (3 hours) and dividing.

questions.question: A boat with speed 8 km/hr in still water goes to a place 30 km away and back in a stream of 2 km/hr. How long does the round trip take?
questions.explanation: Downstream: 30 ÷ 10 = 3 hr. Upstream: 30 ÷ 6 = 5 hr. Total = 8 hr.
questions.method: Time each leg separately and add.

hints.text: Find each leg's speed first.
The trip is not simply 60 ÷ 8.

commonMistakes: Using 60 ÷ 8 = 7.5, ignoring the stream; giving only one leg.

questions.question: A stream flows at 5 km/hr. A boat takes twice as long to go a distance upstream as to come back downstream. What is the boat's speed in still water, in km/hr?
questions.explanation: Same distance, twice the time upstream means the upstream speed is half the downstream speed: b − 5 = (b + 5) ÷ 2. So 2b − 10 = b + 5 and b = 15.
solutionSteps: Twice the time → half the speed: U = D ÷ 2.
questions.method: Equal distance: time and speed are inversely proportional.

hints.text: For the same distance, twice the time means what for the speed?
Write b − 5 = (b + 5) ÷ 2.

commonMistakes: Treating time and speed as directly proportional.

questions.question: A rower goes 20 km upstream in 4 hours and returns downstream in 2 hours. What is the speed of the stream?
questions.explanation: Upstream = 5 km/hr, downstream = 10 km/hr. Stream = (10 − 5) ÷ 2 = 2.5 km/hr.
questions.method: Half the difference of the speeds.

hints.text: Get both speeds first.
The stream is half their difference.

commonMistakes: Giving the full difference (5) or the boat speed (7.5).

questions.question: The stream flows at 3 km/hr. A boat goes 36 km upstream and 36 km back in a total of 5 hours. What is its speed in still water?
questions.method: Substitute each option and check the total time.

hints.text: Solving algebraically leads to a quadratic. Try substituting the options instead.
For each option, add up the two leg times.

commonMistakes: Stopping at an option that only fits one leg.

questions.question: A boat with speed 9 km/hr in still water goes a certain distance downstream and returns, in a stream of 3 km/hr. What is its average speed for the whole round trip?
questions.explanation: Speeds are 12 and 6. Average = 2 × 12 × 6 ÷ (12 + 6) = 144 ÷ 18 = 8 km/hr — lower than 9 because more time is spent on the slow leg.

hints.text: Equal distances each way — is the average speed the simple average of 12 and 6?
More time is spent on the slow leg.

commonMistakes: Giving the still-water speed 9, which is the simple average.

questions.question: A boat goes 28 km downstream in the same time it takes to go 20 km upstream. The stream flows at 3 km/hr. What is the boat's speed in still water?
questions.explanation: Equal times: 28 ÷ (b + 3) = 20 ÷ (b − 3). So 28b − 84 = 20b + 60, giving b = 18 km/hr. Check: 28 ÷ 21 = 20 ÷ 15 = 4/3 hr.
questions.method: Equal times: cross-multiply the two distance ÷ speed expressions.

hints.text: Time is the same, so distance ÷ speed is the same both ways.
Cross-multiply and solve for b.

commonMistakes: Mixing up which leg has b + 3 and which b − 3.

questions.question: A boat's speed in still water is 4 times the speed of the stream. The boat goes 45 km upstream in 5 hours. How long will it take to go 60 km downstream?
questions.explanation: Upstream speed = 45 ÷ 5 = 9 km/hr. If the stream is s, the boat is 4s, so upstream = 4s − s = 3s = 9 and s = 3 km/hr. The boat is 12 km/hr, so downstream = 12 + 3 = 15 km/hr. Time for 60 km = 60 ÷ 15 = 4 hours.
questions.method: Turn the given trip into the upstream speed, then split it into boat and stream.

hints.text: Upstream speed comes straight from 45 km in 5 hours.
Write the upstream speed in terms of the stream speed s.
Downstream speed = boat + stream.

commonMistakes: Dividing 60 by the still-water speed 12 (5 hours).
Taking 9 km/hr as the boat's still-water speed.

questions.question: A man rows to a place 48 km away and back in 14 hours in all. He finds that he can row 4 km downstream in the same time as 3 km upstream. What is the speed of the stream, in km/hr?
questions.explanation: Rowing 4 km downstream takes as long as 3 km upstream, so downstream : upstream speed = 4 : 3. Write them as 4k and 3k. The round trip: 48/(4k) + 48/(3k) = 12/k + 16/k = 28/k = 14, so k = 2. Downstream = 8 km/hr, upstream = 6 km/hr, and the stream = (8 − 6) ÷ 2 = 1 km/hr.
solutionSteps: Equal times: downstream : upstream = 4 : 3, so speeds 4k and 3k.
questions.method: Use the equal-time fact to get the speed ratio, then the round-trip time to scale it.

hints.text: In equal times, distances are in the ratio of speeds.
Write downstream and upstream speeds as 4k and 3k.
Stream speed is half the difference of the two speeds.

commonMistakes: Giving the boat's still-water speed (7 km/hr).
Using the full difference, 2 km/hr, as the stream speed.
